item.title: Obsidian Gains Local REST API with MCP Server for Secure Vault Access
item.description:
Obsidian Gains Local REST API with MCP Server for Secure Vault Access

A new plugin provides a secure REST API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Obsidian vaults, enabling scripts, browser extensions, and AI agents to interact directly with vault contents.

🔍 Overview

The plugin exposes a secure, authenticated REST API alongside an MCP server, both serving the same core capabilities. All requests are served over HTTPS with a locally generated certificate and gated behind API key authentication.

🧩 How it works

The MCP server runs at https://127.0.0.1:27124/mcp/ and requires a bearer token in the Authorization header. A plain HTTP endpoint is also available at http://127.0.0.1:27123/mcp/ if enabled.

⚙️ Key details

  • Authentication: HTTPS with locally generated certificate, API key authentication, bearer token for MCP clients
  • Certificate: CA is name-constrained to localhost, 127.0.0.1, and configured hostnames; HTTP endpoint available for easier setup
  • Download CA: Certificate authority available at https://127.0.0.1:27134/obsidian-local-rest-api.crt
  • Vault operations: Full CRUD on any file including binary files, surgically patch specific sections (headings, blocks, frontmatter), search with full-text or JsonLogic queries, follow vault events via Server-Sent Events
  • Active file: Read or write the currently open note in Obsidian
  • Commands: List and execute any Obsidian command, query tags with usage counts, open specific files in UI
  • Extensibility: Other plugins can register their own routes via an API extension interface

🚀 Availability

After installing and enabling the plugin, users can find their API key and certificate in Settings → Local REST API.

#Obsidian #RESTAPI #MCP #Vault #Plugin

Source: coddingtonbear/obsidian-local-rest-api

item.title: Claude Code edits Obsidian vaults directly via file system
item.description:
Claude Code edits Obsidian vaults directly via file system

Claude Code can edit an Obsidian vault without a special plugin. Because an Obsidian vault is just a local folder of plain‑text .md files, the agent reads and writes those files directly.

🔍 Overview

  • No magical integration; works because the vault is a folder with .md files.
  • No official API, secret API, or mandatory plugin.

🧩 How it works

  • Claude Code runs in a terminal opened inside the vault folder.
  • The agent can create a note, rewrite a note, and add wikilinks directly in the vault.
  • Actions require tool approval (Read, Edit, Write) or can be auto‑approved with acceptEdits mode.
  • Edits can be undone with the /rewind command.

⚙️ Key details

  • Vault: a folder on the file system.
  • Notes: individual .md files, plain text, markdown syntax.
  • Configuration: JSON files in .obsidian inside the vault; plugins store their data.json in their own folders.
  • Internal links: use the wikilink syntax [[link]]; the graph view is just brackets in files.
  • Obsidian behavior: detects external saves and reindexes the note automatically, even while the app is open.
  • Concurrent edits: unsaved changes are merged automatically; Obsidian shows an external‑modification warning.
  • Permissions: the agent is limited to the working directory and its subfolders; writing elsewhere needs explicit permission.
  • No need to close Obsidian each time the agent runs.

🚀 Usage tips

  • Open a terminal in the vault directory, start Claude Code, and treat the vault as a set of markdown files.
  • Enable acceptEdits to stop prompting for each file change.
  • Use /rewind to revert unwanted edits.

#Obsidian #ClaudeCode #AIAgents #Productivity

Source: Claude Code Obsidian: como o agente edita seu vault
